pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test 'AC-1' asserts existing rows are [0,0,0] and that the CHECK rejects 2.
test 'AC-2' checks ★ before the starred item only, in the full list.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1, then checks the starred view returns them in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all return all items in id order.

The code renders the links, but the follow-up commit 07a398e renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test names AC-5 now, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit (07a398e, by a bot) removed the AC-5 label from the link test's title. No test now names AC-5, so the item fails the 'each item is named by its test' rule. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and lists no such edit.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'. Say in the PR why the commit touched the test.

findings.what: The route regex now accepts any query string, which is wider than this change needs. The PR does disclose it.
findings.fix: None needed. Optionally mention that the PR's test-count claim excludes the new traffic-config tests.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter.
All four rows of the state table have a test. AC-5 is no longer named by any test, because a late commit renamed it.
The assertions check behaviour. I did not run the tests: they need the Workers vitest pool and CI runs them.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The traffic README text is still accurate.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is rejected. The SQL is built only from fixed strings.
The show value is never interpolated into SQL or HTML, and titles are escaped. The repository text contains no reviewer-directed instructions.
The HTML page is minimal, with no stylesheet or UI component files in the diff.
No UI components are in the diff, and the PR says no browser was available.
'Changed after the go: nothing' is true of the spec. The AC-5 test rename is not mentioned.
